analysis.investment_thesis: Optiemus is a messy turnaround in low-margin electronics distribution/contract manufacturing, trading at a punishing P/E of 55.6x with a PEG ratio near 2.5 — far too expensive for a business with 5.28% operating margins. The nine-year revenue CAGR of -0.2% and persistently negative free cash flow signal a story I cannot confidently own.
key_strengths: Turnaround recovery is real — revenue rebounded from INR 182 Cr (2021) to INR 1,890 Cr (2025) with EBITDA inflecting positive
Low D/E of 0.32 gives balance sheet headroom; fresh equity raise (financing CF +178 Cr in FY25) strengthens equity base to INR 715 Cr
Pivot into drones, hearables, and IT hardware manufacturing rides 'Make in India' tailwinds
key_risks: PEG ratio ~2.5 (P/E 55.6 ÷ ~22% recent earnings growth) — massively overvalued for the growth on offer
Razor-thin operating margins (5.28%) with no structural moat in commoditized contract manufacturing/distribution
Negative FCF two years running (-INR 96 Cr FY25, -21 Cr FY24) with OCF of -13 Cr in FY25 despite INR 63 Cr net profit — poor earnings quality
red_flags: FY2021 'net profit' of INR 95 Cr was entirely driven by INR 206 Cr 'other income' while operating loss was -98 Cr — the core business was losing money throughout the turnaround
Revenue collapsed 90% from INR 1,922 Cr (2016) to INR 182 Cr (2021), exposing extreme customer/product concentration risk (likely Blackberry distribution loss)
Borrowings surging — up from INR 43 Cr (2022) to INR 247 Cr (2025) — while FCF is deeply negative; capex of INR 83 Cr in FY25 unaccompanied by operational cash generation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my vantage point, Optiemus is a turnaround stock — and turnarounds are my bread and butter, but only when the price is right. The story here is a company that lost its primary distribution franchise (BlackBerry handsets) and saw revenue evaporate 90% over five years, then rebuilt by pivoting into contract manufacturing of wearables, drones, and IT hardware. The recovery is real — revenue has nearly recovered to 2016 levels and EBITDA is now positive at INR 131 Cr. But the market is pricing this as if the hard work is already done: at 55.6x earnings and 33x EV/EBITDA for a business with 5.28% operating margins, there is almost no margin of safety. My PEG calculation comes out to roughly 2.5, and I never want to pay more than 1.0 for a stock like this.

The cash flow picture is the tell. A business earning INR 63 Cr in reported net profit but burning INR 96 Cr in free cash flow is waving a red flag. Operating cash flow turned negative in FY25 (-13 Cr) despite rising profits, which suggests working capital is consuming the business as it scales. The 9-year net profit CAGR of 19.2% is misleading — it's anchored to a tiny 2016 base of INR 13 Cr and includes a one-time INR 206 Cr 'other income' windfall in 2021. ROE at 11.6% sits just below my 12% floor, and margins show no sign of expanding meaningfully. I'd want to see two to three years of positive FCF and a P/E closer to 25-30x before revisiting — at INR 414, this is not a price where good stories become great investments.
